about: Testset for the judge that reads a student's reasoning on a multiple-choice question and returns a verdict (sound, flawed or missing) plus, when flawed, a misconception label. Every item uses a real question from the hosted question bank (curriculum class-10-physics, verified MCQs); question text, options and correct indexes are copied unchanged. The reasoning was written by hand without looking at the judge's prompt or code, in the short, informal style of Class 10 students, in English or Hinglish in Roman script, with spelling slips left in. expectedMisconception is copied verbatim from that question's option_misconceptions when the verdict is flawed, and is null otherwise. Categories: wrong-option-flawed-english and wrong-option-flawed-hinglish (wrong answer, reasoning shows a known misconception, sometimes on an option with no label), right-option-flawed-reasoning (right answer for a wrong reason), right-option-sound (false-alarm check), wrong-option-sound-slip (correct idea, careless arithmetic, unit or selection slip; must not be labelled), and vague (no usable reasoning; expected missing even when the chosen option has a label). topicMisconceptions lists the distinct non-empty option_misconceptions for every topic of the curriculum.

items.question: A wire is cut into two equal halves. What is the resistivity of each half?
options: The same as the original wire
Half of the original
Double the original
One-fourth of the original
items.reasoning: resistivity depends on the length of the wire, if we cut it in half the length becomes half so resistivity also becomes half
items.note: Treats resistivity as if it scaled with length like resistance does.

items.question: Why are household appliances connected in parallel rather than in series?
options: Parallel connection increases the total resistance and saves electricity
The same current then flows through every appliance
Each appliance gets the full mains voltage and can be switched on or off independently
Series wiring would need more wire
items.reasoning: in parallel all the apliances get the same current so every one works properly and none of them gets less current than the other
items.note: Believes parallel branches share one equal current.

items.question: The image formed on the retina of the human eye is
options: virtual and erect
real and inverted
real and erect
virtual and inverted
items.reasoning: we see everything the right way up not upside down, so the image on the retina has to be erect. and its not on a screen so virtual
items.expectedMisconception: Image on the retina is upright
items.note: Infers an upright retinal image from upright perception.

items.topicName: Force on a current in a field
items.question: The direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is given by
options: Fleming's left-hand rule
Fleming's right-hand rule
the right-hand thumb rule
Snell's law
items.reasoning: for force on a conductor we use the right hand rule, thumb is force, first finger is field and middle finger is current
items.expectedMisconception: Uses a right-hand rule for the force
items.note: Uses the right hand for the motor-effect force.

items.question: A second, identical prism is placed upside down after the first prism. What comes out of the second prism?
options: An even wider spectrum
New colours made by the second prism
White light, because the colours recombine
Only red light, because red bends the most
items.reasoning: each prism makes colours out of the light, so the 2nd prism will make more colours again and the band will be even wider
items.note: Chosen option carries no label; the misconception shows only in the reasoning.

items.question: A ray strikes a plane mirror making an angle of 30° with the mirror surface. What is the angle of reflection?
items.reasoning: angle of incidence = angle of refelction. the ray makes 30 with the mirror so it reflects at 30 also
items.expectedMisconception: Measures angles from the mirror surface
items.note: Takes the 30 degrees from the surface as the angle of incidence.

items.question: The clear sky appears blue because
options: it reflects the colour of the oceans
air molecules scatter blue light more than red light
air molecules scatter red light more than blue light
the Sun gives out mostly blue light
items.reasoning: sky blue isliye dikhta h kyuki earth pe zyada tar samundar hai aur uska colour blue hai, sky usi ko reflect karta hai
items.expectedMisconception: Sky is blue because it reflects the sea
items.note: Explains the blue sky as a reflection of the ocean.

items.question: The potential difference across an ohmic resistor is doubled at constant temperature. What happens?
options: The resistance doubles and the current stays the same
Both the current and the resistance double
The current doubles and the resistance stays the same
The current halves
items.reasoning: V = IR hai na, toh V double kiya toh R bhi double ho jayega aur current utna hi rahega
items.note: Reads V = IR as R following V.

items.question: The far point of a myopic person is 80 cm in front of the eye. What is the power of the lens needed to correct this?
items.reasoning: P = 1/f = 1/0.8 = 1.25 D. myopia me convex lens lagate h toh power positive hogi
items.expectedMisconception: Myopia is corrected with a convex lens
items.note: Arithmetic is right; the sign comes from the wrong lens type.

items.question: What is the job of the earth wire on a metal-bodied appliance?
options: It carries current back to the mains during normal use
It provides a low-resistance path to the ground if the body becomes live, protecting the user
It increases the voltage supplied to the appliance
The appliance needs it to work at all
items.reasoning: earth wire se current wapas mains me jata hai, live se aata h aur earth se wapas jata h, isliye teen wire hote h
items.expectedMisconception: Earth wire carries current in normal use
items.note: Treats the earth wire as the normal return path.

items.question: A solenoid with a soft-iron core is used as an electromagnet. When the current is switched off, the core
options: loses almost all of its magnetism
remains a strong permanent magnet
swaps its north and south poles
becomes a stronger magnet
items.reasoning: ek baar iron ke andar magnetism aa gaya toh woh rehta hai, current band karne se thodi na chala jayega
items.expectedMisconception: An electromagnet stays magnetised when switched off
items.note: Expects soft iron to keep its magnetism.

items.question: Stars appear to twinkle because
options: starlight is refracted by air layers whose refractive index keeps changing
stars give out light in pulses
clouds keep passing in front of them
air cannot bend light, so we see their true flicker
items.reasoning: hawa light ko mod nahi sakti toh twinkle ka reason clouds hi hoga jo beech beech me aate h
items.note: Chosen option carries no label; the misconception shows only in the reasoning.

items.question: You shift your gaze from a distant tree to a book in your hands. How does the eye adjust?
options: The eye lens moves closer to the retina
The pupil gets larger to bring the book into focus
The eye lens becomes thinner
The ciliary muscles contract, so the eye lens becomes thicker
items.reasoning: the lens becomes thicker and it also moves forward towards the book so the image comes on the retina
items.expectedMisconception: Eye focuses by moving the lens
items.note: Right answer, but adds lens movement as part of accommodation.

items.question: Two ammeters are placed just before and just after a bulb in a simple circuit. The first reads 0.4 A. What does the second read?
options: Less than 0.4 A, because the bulb used up some current
0 A, because the bulb used up all the current
More than 0.4 A
items.reasoning: bulb thoda sa current use karta h light banane ke liye but itna kam ki ammeter me fark nahi aayega, isliye 0.4 hi
items.expectedMisconception: Current gets used up by components
items.note: Right answer, but still believes the bulb consumes current.

items.question: The Sun looks reddish at sunrise and sunset because
options: light travels a longer path through air, so most blue light is scattered away and mostly red reaches us
red light is scattered the most, towards us
the Sun is cooler in the morning and evening
the ocean reflects red light upwards
items.reasoning: at sunrise the light comes thru more air, and red is scattered the most so it spreads all over and reaches our eyes, thats why sun looks red
items.expectedMisconception: Red light is scattered the most
items.note: Right answer, but reverses which colour scatters most.

items.question: A ray of light travels obliquely from air into glass. At the surface it
options: bends away from the normal
bends towards the normal
goes straight on, since its speed does not change
is completely reflected
items.reasoning: glass is denser so the ray bends towards normal. the speed of light stays same only the direction changes
items.expectedMisconception: Light's speed is the same in every medium
items.note: Right answer, but denies the change of speed that causes refraction.

items.question: The refractive index of diamond is 2.42. This means
options: light travels in vacuum 2.42 times faster than in diamond
light travels 2.42 times faster in diamond than in vacuum
diamond is 2.42 times heavier than glass
light bends by 2.42° inside diamond
items.reasoning: diamond is very heavy and dense, more mass so light slows down 2.42 times inside it
items.note: Right answer, but ties refractive index to mass density.

items.question: You stand 2 m in front of a plane mirror. How far is your image from you?
options: 2 m
4 m
1 m
0 m, it is on the mirror
items.reasoning: image mirror pe hi banti hai 2 m pe, light wahan tak jaati h aur wapas aati h toh 2+2 = 4 m
items.expectedMisconception: Image forms on the mirror surface
items.note: Right number reached by placing the image on the mirror and doubling the light path.

items.question: A material is chosen for a fuse wire because it has
options: a low melting point, so it melts when too much current flows
a high melting point, so it never melts
zero resistance
a high melting point and very low resistance
items.reasoning: fuse ka kaam hai zyada current aane pe pighal jana aur circuit tod dena, isliye low melting point chahiye
items.note: Correct idea: the fuse must melt on overload.

items.question: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines run from
options: the north pole to the south pole
the south pole to the north pole
the middle of the magnet to its ends
nowhere; the field exists only on the drawn lines
items.reasoning: outside the magnet field lines go from north to south, thats the way the north end of a compass points. inside they go s to n
items.note: Correct, including the direction inside the magnet.

items.question: A 2 Ω and an 8 Ω resistor are connected in parallel across a 4 V battery. What current flows through the 2 Ω resistor?
options: 2 A
1.25 A, the same as in the 8 Ω branch
items.reasoning: in parallel both resistors get the full 4V, so I = V/R = 4/2 = 2 A for the 2 ohm one
items.note: Correct use of full voltage across each parallel branch.

items.topicName: Field due to a straight current
items.question: A compass near a straight wire deflects to the east when current flows. The current is then reversed. What does the needle do?
options: It deflects to the west
It keeps deflecting east, because the wire is now magnetised
It points along the wire
It stays still because only the current's size matters
items.reasoning: current ulta kiya toh magnetic field ki direction bhi ulti ho jayegi (right hand thumb rule), toh needle west me jayegi
items.note: Correct: the field reverses with the current.

items.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. Where is the image formed?
options: 30 cm behind the mirror
10 cm in front of the mirror
30 cm in front of the mirror
15 cm in front of the mirror
items.reasoning: u = -30, f = -15. 1/v = 1/f - 1/u = -1/15 + 1/30 = -1/30 so v = -30 cm, in front of the mirror. object is at C so image also at C
items.note: Correct mirror formula with sign convention.

items.question: Half of a convex lens is covered with black paper. What happens to the image of an object?
options: It disappears
It shows only half of the object
It is complete but less bright
It becomes twice as large
items.reasoning: every part of the lens makes the full image, covering half just lets less light thru so its dimmer but still complete
items.note: Correct: each part of the lens forms the whole image.

items.question: A charge of 60 C flows through a wire in 2 minutes. What is the current?
options: 2 A
items.reasoning: I = Q/t, Q = 60 C aur t = 2 toh 60/2 = 30 A
items.note: Right formula; forgot to turn 2 minutes into 120 s.

items.question: A current of 2 A flows through a 5 Ω resistor for 10 s. How much heat is produced?
items.note: Right formula (current squared); dropped the time factor.

items.question: A 1000 W heater is used for 2 hours a day for 30 days. How much energy does it use?
options: 60 kWh
2 kWh
60 kW
items.reasoning: energy = power x time = 1000 x 2 x 30 = 60000 kWh
items.note: Right idea (energy = power x time); left the power in W instead of kW.

items.question: A 4 Ω and a 2 Ω resistor are connected in series to a 12 V battery. What is the potential difference across the 4 Ω resistor?
options: 12 V, because each series resistor gets the full battery voltage
4 V
6 V
8 V
items.reasoning: total R = 4+2 = 6 ohm, I = 12/6 = 2 A. 4 ohm wale pe V = IR = 2 x 2 = 4 V
items.note: Right method; used the 2 ohm value in the last step.

items.question: A convex lens has a focal length of 25 cm. What is its power?
items.reasoning: f = 25 cm = 0.25 m, P = 1/f = 1/0.25 = 4 D. convex lens so its +4
items.note: Reasoning says +4 D but the chosen option is -4 D, whose option carries a label; the label must not be assigned.

items.question: The speed of light in a medium is 2 × 10⁸ m/s. Taking c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s, what is its refractive index?
items.note: Computed 1.5 correctly but selected 1.33.

items.question: When white light passes through a glass prism, a band of colours is seen. Why?
options: The prism adds colours to the white light
White light is made of colours that bend by different amounts
The prism reflects only coloured light
The glass heats up and gives out colours
items.reasoning: we did this in class
items.note: No physics stated; right option.

items.question: Which statement about potential difference is correct?
options: It is the amount of charge flowing past a point each second
It is the work done per unit charge in moving charge between two points
It flows through a resistor and is used up there
A voltmeter must have very low resistance
items.reasoning: just guessed tbh
items.note: Guess on a labelled wrong option; the option label alone is not evidence.

items.question: An ammeter is used to measure the current through a resistor. How should it be connected, and what kind of resistance should a good ammeter have?
options: In series with the resistor, with very low resistance
In parallel with the resistor, with very high resistance
In series with the resistor, with very high resistance
In parallel with the resistor, with very low resistance
items.reasoning: pata nahi yaar, yehi sahi laga
items.note: Feeling only, on a labelled wrong option.

items.question: Where is the magnetic field of a bar magnet strongest?
options: Where the field lines are farthest apart
Where the field lines cross each other
Where the field lines are closest together, near the poles
At the middle of the magnet, between the lines
items.reasoning: its obvious
items.note: No reason given; right option.

items.question: A concave mirror produces a magnification m = −2. This means the image is
options: virtual, erect and twice the size of the object
real, inverted and twice the size of the object
real, inverted and half the size of the object
virtual and half the size of the object
items.reasoning: formula se aaya
items.note: Names no formula or step, on a labelled wrong option.

items.question: Two resistors are connected in parallel across a battery. A third resistor is then connected in parallel with them. What happens to the equivalent resistance of the combination?
options: It decreases
It increases
It stays the same, because the voltage across each resistor is unchanged
It increases if the new resistor is larger than the others, and decreases if it is smaller
items.reasoning: sir ne bataya tha aise hi hota h
items.note: Appeal to the teacher with no reason, on a labelled wrong option.
